author: operator-approved (style revision applied Phase 14A)
author_confidence: high — this is the defect Phase 5 produced and the correction is the point of including it
constraints: The list holds between 2 and 1000 integers. Each value is between 1 and 1000 inclusive.
edge_cases: When every value is identical the smallest and largest are the same number, and the answer is that number. A list containing 1 always yields 1 because 1 divides everything.
input_semantics: One parameter, nums, a list of positive integers. The list may be in any order and may contain repeated values.
load_bearing: Exactly two values participate: the smallest value present and the largest value present. Every other element of the list is ignored, including any element lying between them. The answer is the greatest common divisor of that single pair.
method_behaviour: The method accepts the list and returns one integer. It does not print, does not mutate the input, and does not return a list.
objective: Given a list of positive integers, report the greatest common divisor of exactly two of them: the smallest value present and the largest value present.
output_semantics: A single integer: the greatest common divisor of the smallest and largest values in nums.
required_operation: Find the minimum element and the maximum element of the list, then compute the greatest common divisor of those two numbers only.

revision.rationale: Operator adopted the proposed style revision in Phase 14 (decision 4). Meta-commentary and negative-only phrasing removed; the operation is unchanged: GCD(min(nums), max(nums)), NOT GCD(all nums).
